what_its_for: This medicine is used to treat tension headaches. It contains three ingredients that work together: butalbital relaxes muscle contractions that cause headache pain, acetaminophen (like Tylenol) relieves pain and reduces fever, and caffeine helps the other medicines work better and can help relieve headache pain on its own.
how_to_take: Take this medicine exactly as your doctor prescribed. Swallow the tablet or capsule whole with a full glass of water. You can take it with or without food, but if it upsets your stomach, try taking it with food or milk. Do not crush, chew, or break the tablets or capsules unless your doctor or pharmacist says it is okay. Do not take more than prescribed, and do not take it more often than directed. Using this medicine too often (more than 2 to 3 days per week) can actually cause more headaches, called 'medication overuse headaches' or 'rebound headaches.'
dosing: The usual adult dose is 1 to 2 tablets or capsules every 4 hours as needed for headache pain. Do not take more than 6 tablets or capsules in one day (24 hours). Do not take more than 4,000 mg of acetaminophen total per day from all sources, including other over-the-counter pain medicines, cold medicines, or sleep aids that may also contain acetaminophen. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as your dose may be different.
missed_dose: This medicine is taken only when you have a headache, so it is not taken on a regular daily schedule. Because of this, there is no 'missed dose' to worry about. Never take a double dose to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure when to take your next dose, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store this medicine at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet. Ask your pharmacist about the best way to safely dispose of any medicine you no longer need.
what_to_avoid: Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine. Mixing alcohol with acetaminophen can seriously damage your liver, and mixing alcohol with butalbital can cause dangerous drowsiness and slow your breathing. Avoid driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing anything that requires you to be alert until you know how this medicine affects you, because it can cause drowsiness or dizziness. Avoid taking other medicines that contain acetaminophen (such as Tylenol, NyQuil, Dayquil, or many cold and flu medicines) to prevent accidentally taking too much acetaminophen, which can harm your liver. Avoid other sedatives, sleeping pills, anti-anxiety medicines, opioid pain medicines, or muscle relaxers unless your doctor approves, as these can cause dangerous levels of drowsiness. Limit caffeine from other sources such as coffee, tea, energy drinks, and soda, as extra caffeine may cause jitteriness or trouble sleeping.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or get emergency help if you experience: yellowing of your skin or the whites of your eyes, dark urine, severe stomach pain, or loss of appetite (these may be signs of liver damage); unusual drowsiness, confusion, slow or shallow breathing, or difficulty waking up; signs of an allergic reaction such as skin rash, hives, swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat, or difficulty breathing; if you feel you are becoming dependent on this medication or are taking it very frequently; if your headaches are getting worse or happening more often; or if you notice unusual bleeding, bruising, or signs of infection. Also tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant.
when_it_works: This medicine usually begins to relieve headache pain within 30 to 60 minutes after you take it. It works best when taken at the first sign of a headache, before the pain becomes severe. If you wait until the headache is very bad, it may not work as well.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and older): This medicine should be used with extra caution in older adults because butalbital can cause more dizziness, confusion, and fall risk in this age group. A lower dose may be recommended. Children: This medicine is generally not recommended for children unless specifically prescribed by a doctor. Pregnancy: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Butalbital may cause withdrawal symptoms in newborns if used regularly near the end of pregnancy. Breastfeeding: This medicine can pass into breast milk and may harm a nursing baby. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding while taking this medicine. Liver or kidney problems: Use with caution if you have liver or kidney disease. Your doctor may need to adjust your dose or choose a different medicine. History of substance use disorder: Because butalbital can be habit-forming, people with a history of drug or alcohol addiction should discuss this carefully with their doctor before using this medicine.
